q.q: In the Schatzker classification, which type involves the medial plateau and is associated with high-energy injury, knee dislocation equivalents and risk to the popliteal artery and peroneal nerve?
q.e: Type IV involves the medial plateau and is associated with high-energy injury, knee dislocation equivalents and risk to the popliteal artery and peroneal nerve.
q.src: Type IV involves the medial plateau and is associated with high-energy injury, knee dislocation equivalents and risk to the popliteal artery and peroneal nerve.

q.q: Surgery for a tibial plateau fracture is indicated when articular step-off exceeds:
q.e: Articular step-off over 2 mm or condylar widening over 5 mm, and varus or valgus instability over 10 degrees in extension, are commonly cited indications for surgery.
q.src: Articular step-off over 2 mm or condylar widening over 5 mm, and varus or valgus instability over 10 degrees in extension, are commonly cited indications for surgery.

q.q: Internal fixation is indicated when the displacement of a fracture exceeds:
q.e: Displacement over 1 mm is an indication for internal fixation.
q.src: Displacement over 1 mm is an indication for internal fixation.

q.q: Scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse (SNAC) wrist begins with arthritis at the:
q.e: Scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse (SNAC) wrist begins with arthritis at the radial styloid.
q.src: Scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse (SNAC) wrist begins with arthritis at the radial styloid.

q.q: In the Schatzker classification, which type is a lateral split-depression, the most common type?
q.e: Type II is a lateral split-depression, the most common type.
q.src: Type II is a lateral split-depression, the most common type.

q.q: Which of the following is the most commonly injured nerve in distal radius fractures?
q.e: Median nerve is the most commonly injured nerve in distal radius fractures
q.src: Median nerve is the most commonly injured nerve in distal radius fractures

q.q: Fill in the blank: Acceptable reduction: radial inclination more than ______, radial height loss less than 5 mm, and dorsal tilt less than 10 degrees
q.e: Acceptable reduction: radial inclination more than 15 degrees, radial height loss less than 5 mm, and dorsal tilt less than 10 degrees
q.src: Acceptable reduction: radial inclination more than 15 degrees, radial height loss less than 5 mm, and dorsal tilt less than 10 degrees

q.q: Chauffeur fracture is a fracture of the:
q.e: Chauffeur fracture is a fracture of the radial styloid
q.src: Chauffeur fracture is a fracture of the radial styloid

q.q: Which part of the bone is most commonly affected by osteosarcoma?
q.e: Most common site of osteosarcoma: Answer: Distal femur
q.src: Most common site of osteosarcoma: Answer: Distal femur

q.src: Gartland classification is used for: Answer: Supracondylar fracture humerus

q.q: Investigation of choice for osteoid osteoma:

q.q: Drug of choice for Paget disease:

q.src: Drug of choice for Paget disease: Answer: Zoledronic acid

q.q: Which nerve is most commonly injured in a supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children?

q.src: Most common nerve injured in supracondylar fracture of humerus in children: Answer: Anterior interosseous nerve
